method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula/token/macro comparison, rule-direction inspection and reverse paraphrase with a freshly checked official Government of Maharashtra mathematics glossary passage; not independent or human review.
scope: The semantic-tableau overview: signed formulas and branching trees, paired decomposition rules and closure, tableau-based derivability and inconsistency, historical contributors, systematic proof construction, model extraction, and the connection to sequent calculus.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Unlike derivation systems arranged from sentences, tableaux operate on signed formulas. A signed formula pairs a truth-value sign, true or false, with a sentence. A tableau is a downward-branching tree beginning with assumptions. Inference rules extend a branch with one or more signed formulas, or add two formulas side by side so that the branch splits and each formula ends one new branch.
samples.checks: The sign-and-sentence pair, both displayed alternatives, downward tree orientation, assumptions, dependence on a formula above, single-branch extension and two-way split are all explicit. Every token, macro and displayed formula remains unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Applying a rule to a complex signed formula adds signed immediate subformulas. Rules occur in true/false pairs. True A-and-B adds both true A and true B on the same branch; the false rule splits a branch with false A and false B side by side. A tableau is closed exactly when every branch contains matching true-A and false-A signed formulas.
samples.checks: The true conjunction rule does not branch; the false conjunction rule does branch. The closure requirement quantifies over every branch and requires the same A with opposite signs. All six rule/formula displays preserve source identity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma proves A by tableaux exactly when some finite Gamma-zero, consisting of B-one through B-n and contained in Gamma, yields a closed tableau from false A together with true B-one through true B-n. The displayed closed tableau establishes that A-and-B implies A.
samples.checks: The finite subset condition, false sign on the goal, true signs on premises, closure requirement and biconditional direction are preserved. Every tableau node, rule justification, numeric reference, formula and close marker is unchanged in the aligned translation source. MRPRF-001 records that the final two source rule labels name the conditional rather than the conjunction being decomposed; the reader projection corrects exactly those labels.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma is inconsistent in the tableau calculus when there is a closed tableau whose assumptions are true B-one through true B-n for source formulas B-i belonging to Gamma.
samples.checks: The source states this as a sufficient condition rather than an iff definition, and the Marathi retains that one-way if-clause. The sign, membership relation, assumption set and closure are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Beth and Hintikka independently invented tableaux in the 1950s, and Smullyan simplified and popularized them. Construction is systematic and easy to implement by computer, though tableaux can be hard to read and their relation to proofs can be unclear. Many logics have tableau systems. A satisfiable sentence set has no closed tableau, so every tableau has an open branch; a satisfying structure can be read from a fully expanded open branch. A closed tableau is essentially a condensed sequent-calculus derivation written upside down.
samples.checks: All three contributors and roles, the usability advantages and limitations, generality across logics, satisfiable-to-open-branch implication, saturation proviso, satisfying-structure extraction, and upside-down sequent-calculus relation are preserved.

source_observations: MRPRF-001: the final two rule labels in the displayed closed tableau say true-conditional although their parent is the true conjunction T(A and B) and their children are T A and T B. Aligned source fidelity is retained; the reader projection uses true-conjunction labels with an editorial disclosure.
limitations: No independent linguistic review has been performed.

The official glossary directly supports चिन्हांकित as a modifier for signed mathematical objects, चिन्ह, and वाक्य, but does not directly attest चिन्हांकित सूत्र or तात्काळ उपसूत्र as complete logic terms.

टॅब्लो, बंद टॅब्लो, खुली शाखा and the Marathi spellings of Evert Beth, Jaakko Hintikka and Raymond Smullyan remain definition-controlled or phonetic provisional decisions exposed for specialist review.
